ESPN released a teaser Thursday for an upcoming E60 episode about veteran NBA guard Ben Simmons entitled "Being Ben."

In a video posted Thursday on X, Simmons was asked when he knew that his time with the Philadelphia 76ers was "going in the wrong direction," and Simmons responded by asking, "The truth?"

Marc J. Spears of ESPN's Andscape, who worked with Simmons on the E60 episode, took to X to write, "Been amazing to work on this E60 . Ben Simmons has been very wide open throughout the whole process. Look forward to it making its debut."

Selected first overall out of LSU by the Sixers in the 2016 NBA draft, Simmons entered the league with a ton of fanfare.

The Aussie enjoyed early success as well, winning NBA Rookie of the Year honors in 2018, and getting selected to the All-Star Game three consecutive seasons from 2019 to 2021, while also earning two nods to the NBA All-Defensive First Team.

However, after he and the top-seeded 76ers disappointed in the playoffs in 2021 by getting knocked out by the Atlanta Hawks in the second round, Simmons was traded to the Brooklyn Nets.

Injuries plagued Simmons over the course of the next several seasons, as he appeared in a total of just 108 regular-season games from 2021 to 2025.

After sitting out last season, Simmons signed with the Sacramento Kings this month, and he is poised to make his NBA comeback during the 2026-27 campaign.

articles.title: El Real Madrid sufre su primera derrota de la temporada en el estreno de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, en un partido a contrapelo, no supieron rematar y Feliz desperdició el último ataque para ganar
articles.summary: Los blancos, en un partido a contrapelo, no supieron rematar y Feliz desperdició el último ataque para ganar
articles.body: El Real Madrid volverá de su paso por los Emiratos con un título, la SuperCup, y una derrota, la primera de la temporada en el estreno de la Euroliga. A los blancos les faltó claridad en el tramo final, no anotaron en los últimos tres minutos y perdieron por 78-77 en su visita al Dubai Basketball, el mismo rival al que superaron en la prórroga en semifinales del primer torneo del curso. Esta vez salió cruz. Andrés Feliz tuvo el último balón para ganar pero, contenido por la buena defensa de Petrusev, se quedó a medias entre un tiro en suspensión y una entrada a canasta. Su lanzamiento a la remanguillé no entró. Ganaron los de Xavi Pascual. Perdieron los de Pedro Martínez, que sufrió su primer tropiezo en partido oficial como entrenador del Madrid. En un duelo de estilos, para los blancos fue un choque a contrapelo. No dominaron el rebote (45-30 concediendo 18 bajo su aro), con lo que no pudieron correr y, en ataque estático, no tuvieron demasiada puntería: 6/18 en triples, pocos lanzamientos para el juego que quieren hacer. Las mejores noticias fueron los galones mostrados por Maledon (11 puntos y seis asistencias), la versatilidad de Jantunen (10) y los buenos minutos de Jones (10 puntos y tres rebotes en el tercer cuarto) ante las faltas de Tavares. Enfrente, Bacon fue un tormento: 24 puntos, cinco rebotes y cuatro asistencias. El Madrid descartó a Llull, Shulga y Okeke, mientras que Nick Smith Jr. aún no está inscrito. La tarde empezó con un primer cuarto sin triples (0/4) y sin una sola asistencia. Venía de dar 55 en los dos partidos de la SuperCup. Acabó con sólo 13. A los cinco minutos sumaban una canasya en juego y un matazo de Bacon puso el 15-7, pero se rehicieron los blancos aceptando el cuerpo a cuerpo propuesto por el rival. En el segundo cuarto se parecieron algo más a sí mismos. Se fueron a los 28 puntos. Jantunen abrió la lata de los triples y se le sumaron Luwawu-Cabarrot y Abalde para firmar un 0-12 que llevó 11 arriba (33-44). Un triple de Kabengele sobre la bocina apretó el marcador. Okobo, inédito hasta entonces, descorchó la segunda parte con seis puntos seguidos. Dubai devolvió el parcial: 14-0 y 47-44. El tercer periodo fue un intercambio constante de golpes con el marcador convertido en un péndulo. Tavares hizo su tercera falta, pero el problema se convirtió en solución por los sensacionales minutos de Jones, jugando por encima del aro y haciéndose fuerte en el rebote. articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "Nuestro último ataque fue terrible"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Real Madrid lamenta el mal juego de su equipo en el tramo final, especialmente en la posesión que desperdició Feliz
articles.summary: El técnico del Real Madrid lamenta el mal juego de su equipo en el tramo final, especialmente en la posesión que desperdició Feliz
articles.body: Pedro Martínez, entrenador del Real Madrid, se mostró crítico tras la derrota por 78-77 ante el Dubai Basketball en el estreno en la Euroliga, marcada por la mala gestión de las últimas posesiones y un último ataque "terrible", protagonizado por Andrés Feliz. "Ha sido un partido muy igualado. Los dos equipos han tenido buenos y malos momentos. Nuestro peor momento ha sido el principio del tercer cuarto en el que perdimos la ventaja que teníamos al descanso. No empezamos bien la segunda parte. Al final del partido no jugamos bien, nuestra defensa no fue suficientemente bien con algunos triples abiertos y en nuestro ataque fallamos bandejas y nuestro último ataque fue terrible", analizó en la rueda de prensa posterior al encuentro. El técnico reconoció la gran defensa "inteligente" de los locales, que propició que el Madrid tuviese problemas para "encontrar a sus tiradores. "El otro día ganamos y hoy perdimos, pero es porque somos equipos muy igualados y tenemos que estar preparados para ganar y perder. Cuando ganas no decir que todo es perfecto y cuando pierdes tampoco decir que todo está mal", dijo en comparación con el duelo en la Supercopa de la Euroliga. Asimismo, señaló el control del rebote ofensivo del Dubai como una de las claves, ya que permitieron que los locales corriesen más y anotasen más puntos. "Hemos recibido más puntos en contraataque de los que hemos hecho, nos han cogido más rebotes en ataque y han metido más triples de los que hemos metido. Hay que analizar por qué han pasado estas cosas pero no es algo que nos parezca bien. Tenemos que mejorar de cara al futuro", advirtió. En esa línea, esperó una mejora y un mayor control en las últimas posesiones, al que acabaron cediendo la victoria tras encadenar demasiados "errores". "Creo que teníamos una buena ventaja para poder ganar pero fallamos algunas bandejas porque no conseguimos buenas situaciones. Dubai tiene una muy buena defensa, pero por otro lado, nuestra defensa en ese tiempo no fue buena. No controlamos por dos veces en los últimos 3 minutos en el rebote defensivo y en el balance permitimos un triple abierto que no pudimos puntear. Esa es la diferencia. Cometimos errores ante un buen equipo y es algo que te hace perder", concluyó.

articles.title: Everything Rob Pelinka and JJ Redick Said About LeBron James' Exit, Luka Doncic, Lakers' Offseason
articles.summary: It will be a new era for the Los Angeles Lakers after LeBron James departed for the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason, but the Purple and Gold are still thankful for their time with the King.
articles.body:
It will be a new era for the Los Angeles Lakers after LeBron James departed for the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason, but the Purple and Gold are still thankful for their time with the King.

"It was a great era, and we're grateful for it," Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka told reporters Thursday.

He also explained James and his agent, Rich Paul, informed Los Angeles they planned on signing elsewhere, which prompted a pivot from the front office to focus elsewhere:

That pivot meant building the roster around Luka Dončić as the clear-cut franchise cornerstone. While Dončić is one of the best players in the league, James casts a large presence as one of the greatest to ever take the court in NBA history.

With the future Hall of Famer now on the 76ers, this is Dončić's team moving forward. And Pelinka addressed what that means:

Head coach JJ Redick also discussed the makeup of this year's team in a post-LeBron world:

Surrounding Dončić with bigs who can catch his lobs and work off his penetration and ball-handling made the most sense, and the Lakers added Walker Kessler in a notable move.

Still, James' departure was the biggest headline of the Lakers' offseason.

After all, he played eight seasons for Los Angeles, which stands as his longest stretch of consecutive years for one team. While he played for the Cleveland Cavaliers for 11 seasons, that was split across two different stints of seven and four years.

Those eight years with the Lakers included the 2020 championship, eight All-Star nods, seven All-NBA selections and him becoming the all-time leading scorer in NBA history.

Whenever someone with a list of accomplishments like that changes teams, it is going to generate headlines.

But Pelinka called the split "amicable" and "respectful," suggesting there is no ill-will on either side.

Attention will eventually turn to the upcoming campaign, which begins on Oct. 21 against the Golden State Warriors. Dončić and Austin Reaves will be the focal point, but the supporting cast's ability to elevate their own games could determine the ceiling for the team.

Along those lines, Redick said "there are a lot of minutes" and "starting spots" for the taking during training camp.

articles.title: Remontada épica del Barça para un triunfo de mucho mérito
articles.standfirst: Llegó a perder por 15 en el arranque ante el Anadolu Efes, hasta que se puso en manos de Brizuela y Punter
articles.summary: Llegó a perder por 15 en el arranque ante el Anadolu Efes, hasta que se puso en manos de Brizuela y Punter
articles.body: El Barcelona remontó una diferencia de 15 puntos en cuarto y medio para llevarse el partido ante el Anadolu Efes en su estreno en la Euroliga, 89-82. Sin sus tres pívots y con el talento de Darío Brizuela y Kevin Punter, los de Sekulic lograron un triunfo de mucho mérito que apuntala, de momento, el nuevo proyecto azulgrana. Amenazaba tormenta y de las gordas en el Palau Blaugrana cuando a 6:10 para el final del primer cuarto el Anadolu Efes arrasaba al Barcelona 4-19. En una puesta en escena surrealista, el equipo de Sekulic se había quedado en el vestuario y llegó tarde al partido. Pero llegó. En un primer arranque de orgullo, el Barça empezó a recortar la diferencia, aunque muy despacio. Llegó al final del primer cuarto por debajo, 13-25, pero mejorando sus sensaciones. Con la llegada del segundo cuarto, la tormenta cambió de nombre (Brizuela) y de dirección. Una canasta de Santi Yusta, que tuvo muy buenos minutos, colocó un 24-36 a 5.02. Desde ahí, un desatado Brizuela guió al Barcelona a una épica remontada dando un recital de talento y liderazgo muy necesario para el equipo de Sekulic. El Barça firmó un parcial de 21-8 para acabar el segundo cuarto con ventaja, 45-44, gracias en parte a que Brizuela firmó 11 de sus 13 puntos al descanso en ese tramo, con excelentes canastas, sobre todo el último triple del primer tiempo. Con el Barça a todo tren, como le gusta a Sekulic que sea su equipo, el Anadolu subsistió al golpe porque en su equipo tienen un tipo como Dario Saric que ha tenido un regreso triunfal a la Euroliga. Se sentó al final del tercer cuarto con 17 puntos y abusando de la debilitada pintura del Barça por las bajas ya conocidas de Tosan Evbuomwan y Yoan Makoundou y la de última hora de Josh Nebo con problemas en el sóleo y que estará fuera entre dos y tres semanas. Cuando el tercer cuarto expiró, el Anadolu Efes mandaba de nuevo en el marcador, 63-67, por una canasta sobre la bocina de Osmani. Pero todo estaba abierto. El partido bajó al barro en el último periodo, se ensució mucho. El Barça tardó seis minutos en recuperar el control del partido, 72-73, cuando volvió Brizuela. El vasco llegó a los 20 puntos con ese triple. Y con otro, su primero del partido, Tyrese Martin puso el 77-77 a 2:30 con todo por decidir. Hasta ese punto, el Barça se había dejado guiar por Brizuela (20 puntos), primero, y por Punter (19 puntos) después. El triple estaba marcando el tono del partido. El Barça estaba en un 11/27 que le daba la vida mientras el Anadolu Efes se estrellaba con un 4/19. Un mate de Balcerowski a pase de Parra colocaba el 83-80 a un minuto para el final. Mike James fallaba un tiros libre de la serie de tres poco después (83-82). Y un triple de Justin Robinson en el siguiente ataque (86-82) daba al Barça cuatro de ventaja. El robo de Punter a James, con quien bromeaba segundos antes, certificó el gran triunfo del Barça. Frustrado, James se ganó una técnica al final demostrando el complicado vestuario con el que va a tener que lidiar Pablo Laso durante toda la temporada.

articles.title: El campeón Olympiacos impone su ley en el Buesa Arena
articles.standfirst: Vezenkov y Dorsey acaban con la resistencia de un Kosner Baskonia muy mermado
articles.summary: Vezenkov y Dorsey acaban con la resistencia de un Kosner Baskonia muy mermado
articles.body: Sasa Vezenkov y Tyler Dorsey impusieron la del campeón este jueves en Vitoria con una cómoda victoria por 89-106, ante un Kosner Baskonia que sufrió en defensa y no pudo contener el talento y el físico de su rival. El ala-pívot búlgaro y el anotador heleno, con 47 puntos entre ambos, se multiplicaron para darle la vuelta a un partido en un primer cuarto de color azulgrana y lanzar a su equipo con contundencia. AJ Lawson con 20 puntos y Tadas Sedekerskis con liderazgo en la pista, fueron los mejores de un Baskonia que tiene mucho trabajo por delante. Los azulgranas comenzaron con mucho acierto y cuatro triples prácticamente consecutivos marcaron un 14-6 de inicio, que obligó a frenar en secó el duelo al técnico griego. Los tres triples de Tadas Sedekerskis fueron contestados por la facilidad anotadora de Sasa Vezenkov y Tyler Dorsey, que mantuvieron en partido a los de El Pireo ante la sangría de triples locales. Dorsey empató el partido con cinco puntos consecutivos tras los errores defensivos baskonistas, que concedieron canastas fáciles a un Olympiacos que no dejó de anotar y cerró el primer asalto con un 3-10, para darle la vuelta al marcador, 29-36. El rebote ofensivo fue un apoyo fundamental para los visitantes que aprovecharon su mayor envergadura. El Baskonia funcionaba mejor en velocidad, con AJ Lawson como estilete, y así recortó distancias, pero apareció Jean Montero para sumarse a la pareja anotadora griega, que dominaba el partido al descanso, 46-56. El intercambio de golpes tras el descanso favoreció a un Olympiacos, que fue poco a poco tirando de talento para abrir aún más la brecha. Dorsey y Vezenkov no dejaron de destrozar el aro baskonista y Paolo Galbiati intentó cambiar el ritmo con una defensa en zona, pero la diferencia se estiró por encima de los 20 puntos, 60-81. Markus Howard dio aire desde el exterior a un Baskonia que sufría en la pintura y que se vio superado en el uno contra uno. articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Reveals What Fever Need to Fix Ahead of 2026 WNBA Playoffs in New Video
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham says the Indiana Fever are ready to learn from what she described as "one of our worst games of the whole season" in Sunday's 93-77 loss to the Washington Mystics.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham says the Indiana Fever are ready to learn from what she described as "one of our worst games of the whole season" in Sunday's 93-77 loss to the Washington Mystics.

The Fever conceded 34 first-quarter points and never led in a loss that put Indiana on track for a lower seed in the 2026 WNBA playoffs.

"It sucks that it happened right now, but at least it happened now and not during playoffs," Cunningham said around the 3:45 mark of Thursday's episode of No Hesitation with Sophie Cunningham & Drew Hanlen. "I think you can still learn from it a little bit."

Cunningham continued around the 8:40 mark, "As a team, in that first quarter— that's something that we've got to get better at. We talk about this all the time. We've got to punch first. We've got to set the tone early."

The Fever shot just 21 percent from behind the arc in Sunday's loss, marking an off night for a team averaging a WNBA-high 39.3 percent shooting rate from deep.

On Thursday's podcast, however, Cunningham said doesn't feel Fever players "live and die by threes."

Cunningham, who podcast co-host Hanlen pointed out is a significantly more efficient shooter when she sees more minutes on the court, said she feels her team's success hinges more on getting depth players involved on offense.

"We had one of the best offenses in WNBA history with the amount of points that we scored this season in a stretch... I think my biggest thing is our ball movement," Cunningham said. "I think it's our assists. I think it's getting involved. I think when we have anywhere from five, to six, to seven people into double figures, and everyone's getting involved... we're phenomenal."

"Do we have a lot of great three-point shooters? Absolutely. But I think it's getting other people involved... that's when we're at our best."

The Fever bounced back from Sunday's loss with a Tuesday blowout against a Minnesota Lynx team that sat starters for the second half.

Indiana is now preparing to close out the regular season Thursday night with a road game at the Lynx. A win would lock the Fever in to the No. 5 seed, per ESPN's Michael Voepel .

A loss combined with a Washington Mystics win over the Chicago Sky would drop the Fever to the No. 6 seed, per Voepel.

Cunningham will hope to see the Fever come out with a stronger start when the regular season finale tips off at 8 p.m. ET in Minneapolis.

articles.title: Sam Presti Says 2026-27 Thunder Have 'A Chance' to Be as Good as 2025 NBA Title Team
articles.summary: Oklahoma City Thunder general manager Sam Presti believes that the 2026-27 roster can be just as successful as the organization's 2025 championship-winning team.
articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder general manager Sam Presti believes that the 2026-27 roster can be just as successful as the organization's 2025 championship-winning team.

"I think the team last year had another level to it," Presti said in a Thursday press conference, via ESPN's Baxter Holmes . "I think we could have got to another level. But I think in due time, like I said earlier, this particular group of players, if we stay healthy, if it has time together, it has a chance to be as good if not better than any of the teams we've had."

Ranking the NBA's Best Young Cores Right Now 🔢

After racking up 68 wins and capturing a title during the 2024-25 season, the Thunder looked to hoist the Larry O'Brien Trophy again after compiling a 64-18 record during their 2025-26 campaign.

Oklahoma City ultimately fell to the San Antonio Spurs in seven games during the Western Conference Finals, though.

The 2026-27 Thunder squad will look slightly different compared to past years, as the front office parted ways with Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins earlier this offseason.

Still, Oklahoma City boasts a talented roster that includes its star trio of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren.

Williams and Holmgren have both earned one All-Star nod since the start of the 2024-25 season, while Gilgeous-Alexander is attempting to become the first player to win three consecutive MVP awards since Larry Bird from 1984-86.

"We have three guys, two of which are not even in their prime, that are All-NBA players, and also the other guy that's a back-to-back MVP [Gilgeous-Alexander], and he's only getting better as well in his prime," Presti said Thursday, per Holmes.

The Thunder also have plenty of capable backcourt options including Ajay Mitchell, Cason Wallace and Jared McCain to go along with a frontcourt rotation featuring Isaiah Hartenstein and Jaylin Williams.

It's worth noting that Mitchell and Jalen Williams were both unable to suit up in Game 7 against San Antonio due to injuries .

It'll be intriguing to see how the Thunder fare against the Spurs and Victor Wembanyama this year, as they went just 4-8 when facing San Antonio during the prior regular season and playoffs.

Even with questions surrounding Oklahoma City's outlook against the Spurs, the Thunder are still entering this season as a top contender to win another championship.

articles.title: Roddy Gayle Jr. gets ruling to play for Michigan basketball in 2026-27
articles.summary: Roddy Gayle Jr., a key member of Michigan basketball's NCAA championship team, was granted a preliminary injunction in Niagara County Supreme Court.
articles.body:
Michigan basketball received its second win in court in as many days on Thursday, Sept. 24.

Roddy Gayle Jr., a key member of the Wolverines ' 2025-26 national championship team, was granted a preliminary injunction in Niagara County Supreme Court by New York Judge Frank A. Sedita III on Thursday, according to online court records . The ruling allows him to remain on the U-M basketball team, despite the NCAA's ruling that he has exhausted his eligibility, until there is a final decision.

Gayle is the second U-M guard to be cleared this week, after Columbia transfer Kenny Noland was granted his injunction one day earlier. Both are among the hundreds of athletes who've sued the NCAA as they seek an extra year of eligibility to match the NCAA's shift to a "five-in-five" system for the class of 2027. Gayle played four seasons – two for Ohio State and two for Michigan – before signing a contract with the Detroit Pistons to play in the Las Vegas Summer League team in August.

Gayle argued in his filing in his home state of New York that he did so only because he felt there was no option for him to return to college, with the NCAA declining to extend the "five-in-five" rule for 2026 seniors.

"I did not leave college for professional basketball," Gayle said in a statement when he filed his lawsuit. "I completed four seasons, I graduated, and the NCAA's new carve-out told me I could not play a fifth. Only then did I turn to professional basketball.

"I have never played in a professional regular-season game, and I have never been paid a salary to play basketball, in any league or any country. … I am not asking the court to order any school to put me on its roster. I am not asking the NCAA for money, and I seek no damages. I am asking only that the NCAA be restrained from declaring me ineligible, from interfering with Michigan's decision to let me play, and from punishing Michigan, its coaches, or my teammates for following this court's order, so that I may compete for a spot on the same terms as every other player."

Michigan basketball 2026-27 roster for title defense

In the ruling allowing Noland to play for U-M – issued in Indiana – Judge Kara Krothe found "under the plain, unambiguous text of the [NCAA] Manual, Plaintiffs are eligible" since the text of the new eligibility bylaw didn't explicitly exclude the class of 2026. The judgment in New York on Gayle was not immediately made public online, outside of his ruling being granted.

Gayle played a career-high 39 games last season, averaging 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 21.1 minutes per game. He played in 146 games across his career, starting 72 games (including 25 for U-M in 2025-26).

This reunion had been in the works for some time, with coach Mike Boynton Jr. saying before the team left for Europe that the group would "welcome Roddy back" if it was possible.

"For sure, I definitely want him to come back," said Elliot Cadeau, Gayle's teammate last season in the backcourt, the same day. "He's a great leader, a great player. He won a national championship. Anybody that won a national championship, we would love to have on the team.

"I hope it's possible. I don't really know (with) the uncertainty of college basketball nowadays. It's something I can't really touch on or know, but I really hope he comes back."

articles.summary: Roddy Gayle Jr.’s quest to secure a fifth season of eligibility and return to Michigan basketball has passed a significant hurdle.

Roddy Gayle Jr.'s quest to secure a fifth season of eligibility and return to Michigan basketball has passed a significant hurdle.

On Thursday, Sept. 24, a New York judge granted Gayle's request for a preliminary injunction in his case against the NCAA, paving the way for him to play for the Wolverines in the 2026-27 season.

Judge Frank Sedita III's ruling comes weeks after Gayle, a New York native who spent the past two seasons at Michigan, filed a lawsuit against the NCAA in Niagara County Supreme Court on Aug. 31 — one of many cases across the country that challenged the NCAA's new five-year eligibility rule that excluded the high school class of 2022.

With a preliminary injunction in place, Gayle can suit up with the Wolverines, though his status could change pending on any further legal action. The NCAA has vowed to fight all federal and state cases filed by athletes seeking a fifth season, and Gayle's case is expected to be appealed.

Still, the ruling is welcome news for a Michigan backcourt that lost star freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. to a torn ACL and lacks proven pieces aside from starters Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney.

Coach Mike Boynton Jr. stated this summer he was open to a reunion with Gayle , depending on what the courts decide. Gayle traveled with Michigan during its 10-day European tour last month, is enrolled at the university and was granted a temporary restraining order Sept. 2 that allowed him to practice with the team until the preliminary injunction hearing — which was originally set for Sept. 17 before being rescheduled.

"If the opportunity presents itself, this is not he's going to go into the market and try to figure out where's the most money he can make," Boynton said of Gayle on the program's "Defend the Block" podcast earlier this month. "He wants to be at Michigan. He feels very much attached and connected to this program and the people he's built a relationship with the last two years, and he wants to be a part of continuing to build what's going to stabilize Michigan for years to come.

"And if he's able to do so, we'd love to have him back. We have had communications with our team about his presence. He's been in this league (Big Ten) for four years. He's been in this program for two years, and he's been one of the guys who's made as many sacrifices as anybody for us to do what ultimately we were able to do the last two years of reestablishing Michigan's presence as a real championship program. We hope that it all works out. … But if it can happen, we want it to happen, and we'd love to have him."

A key reserve on Michigan's national title team last season, Gayle, a 6-foot-5 guard, averaged 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 21.1 minutes per game and shot a career-best 46.3% from the field.

After going undrafted, Gayle signed a Summer League deal with the Detroit Pistons in late June, played in four NBA Summer League games in July and was seemingly set to start a pro career. That was until a federal court ruling in late July granted Gayle and 2022 high school class athletes a fifth year of eligibility — a ruling that has since been halted as the NCAA appeals.

"In fairness to the kid, if he had known that (there'd be a possibility of a fifth year) and he wanted to come back, maybe he would have considered that before playing in Summer League. But that wasn't the information at the time," Boynton said earlier this summer.

"I would hope that if the rules are changed, then they would say he didn't do anything wrong, per se. This wasn't an option, and now it is."

Michigan entered August with two roster spots available and had one remaining after the Aug. 19 addition of guard Kenny Noland, a Columbia transfer who's eligible to play after a circuit court judge in Indiana granted him a preliminary injunction on Wednesday, Sept. 23.

Boynton and other staff members know what they're getting in Gayle, who's been an integral part of the program the last two seasons. He appeared in 39 games with one start last year and started 25 games in 2024-25. For his career, which includes two years at Ohio State, Gayle has played in 146 games with 72 starts.

He's had several standout performances with Michigan in the postseason, which earned him the nickname "March Roddy." During last season's national title run , he had 14 points against Howard in first round, scored 16 against Alabama in the Sweet 16, and made eight 3-pointers at a 53.3% clip in the NCAA Tournament — after making just 13 deep balls the entire regular season.

Gayle's addition would bring a veteran presence to a team that has six freshmen and other unproven players. More importantly, he'd help provide depth and shore up a backcourt that lost guard L.J. Cason to the transfer portal and McCoy to a season-ending knee injury.

"He's a great leader, a great player," Cadeau said of Gayle last month. "He won a national championship. Anybody that won a national championship, we would love to have on the team."

articles.title: Nevada coach Steve Alford to retire after 2026-27 season, ending a 36-year career coaching college basketball
articles.summary: Alford earned 13 NCAA tournament berths, five conference tournament titles and six regular-season championships coaching Missouri State, Iowa, New Mexico, UC...
articles.body:
Nevada men's basketball coach Steve Alford will retire following the 2026-27 season, he announced on Thursday.

The upcoming season will be Alford's eighth with the Wolf Pack, finishing up a 36-year career as a college head coach that included stints at Iowa, New Mexico and UCLA. He won five conference tournament championships, six regular-season titles and 13 NCAA tournament berths.

This story will be updated with more information.
